controls.label: Infrared color
controls.qualification: False color from its measured flux in three infrared bands (Best et al. (2021); McMahon et al. (2013), as compiled in Best, Liu, Magnier & Dupuy (2024), The UltracoolSheet v2.1 (Zenodo); zero points from the SVO Filter Profile Service). The disc itself is unresolved; darkening toward the edge from a model atmosphere.
controls.notes: VHS 1256-1257 b's brightness in three infrared bands as one color: red MKO K 2.184 µm, green MKO H 1.614 µm, blue MKO J 1.2417 µm (Best et al. (2021); McMahon et al. (2013), as compiled in Best, Liu, Magnier & Dupuy (2024), The UltracoolSheet v2.1 (Zenodo); zero points from the SVO Filter Profile Service), on a range shared with this planet alone, from zero to its brightest band (mko k), so the color shows its band ratios; brightness is not compared across planets at different distances. Not a natural color; nobody has resolved its disc. The darkening toward the edge is the quadratic law fitted to the MKO H intensity PICASO 4.1 (Batalha et al. 2019, ApJ 878, 70) computes from Sonora Diamondback cloudy (Morley et al. 2024, ApJ 975, 59; [M/H] +0.5, f_sed 1) model atmospheres at 1,116 K and log g 3.5, read between the models t1100g31f1_m+0.5_co1.0, t1100g100f1_m+0.5_co1.0, t1200g31f1_m+0.5_co1.0, t1200g100f1_m+0.5_co1.0 (u1 0.886, u2 -0.080; the law fits each model's eight angles within 0.07% of the centre): a cloudy model, the one Petrus et al. (2024), ApJL 966, L11 fit to this planet, because no table reaches a planet this cold and nobody has resolved its disc.

physical.credit: Model radius and temperature from the JWST spectrum; orbit refitted with orbitize! on Poon et al.'s (2024) inputs; one of the orbits the measurements allow
